rules.description: Increase in hours -> compared against previous mastery criteria
rules.notes: Previously described as needing 'stored previous-TP data' as if that meant backend-only storage this POC doesn't have. Confirmed against real documents (CS TP.pdf, Reeda Bint Shaheen's TP): the previous authorization's approved hours per CPT code ARE printed directly on the same TP's own page, under 'Hours Approved Previous Authorization:' (e.g. '97153-Direct Care by Behavior Technician 25 hours per week') -- no backend/prior-TP storage needed to read them. Compare each code's current requested hours (from the Hours Requesting section) against that same code's previous-authorization hours in this block; if a code's hours increased, check whether the accompanying clinical-rationale narrative for that code substantively addresses the increase. The data-presence half of this is a plain read; judging whether the rationale text is adequate is the genuinely judgment-based half this rule keeps. TIGHTENED, REAL BAR FOR 'ADEQUATE' (2026-08-08, Round 78, item 3 -- real miss confirmed against Ms. Yachnes's ground-truth review, Yisroel Leibowitz's real TP: the rationale for a 97153 increase cited VB-MAPP score gains and 'mastered goals' generally, and this rule passed it -- but it never named which specific prior mastery criteria the gains were being measured against, and Ms. Yachnes's own bar is that it must). ANY narrative sentence near an hours increase is NOT enough by itself -- a passing rationale must concretely tie the increase to the client's SPECIFIC prior mastery criteria or goals (e.g. naming an actual goal, a specific mastery percentage/criterion reached or still outstanding, a named skill domain from the mastered/in-progress goals lists) -- not just general language like 'continued need due to progress,' 'client has shown improvement,' or a score/assessment result cited without connecting it to a specific goal or criterion. FAIL example (real, from this round's ground-truth miss): 'client has made gains on the VB-MAPP and mastered several goals, and continued intensive treatment is recommended to build on this progress' -- describes general progress, never names which mastered goal(s) or which specific mastery criteria the increase is measured against. PASS example: 'the increase to 31 hrs/week reflects the client's mastery of the 3 manding goals (mastery criteria: 80% across 3 consecutive sessions) and the need for expanded direct-hours to address the 2 new goals added to target receptive language, per the current Goals in Progress list' -- names specific goals/criteria the increase is tied to. When in doubt whether a rationale is concrete enough, prefer 'uncertain' over a guessed pass -- this bar is about genuine specificity, not phrasing style.

rules.description: Overlap with home health aide/speech/OT -> goals differentiated
rules.notes:
Semantic check that TP explains how ABA goals differ from the other service.

RECALIBRATED (2026-08, Round 82, item 4): confirmed real case -- a patient receiving school-based Speech/OT (different setting, different provider type, IEP-driven) alongside home-based ABA was failed for not containing an explicit sentence stating how ABA goals differ from speech/OT, even though the services are self-evidently different in scope/setting/discipline. Investigated both directions honestly: this is a genuine calibration gap, NOT a case where the original grader was right to fail it outright -- but it is also NOT simply 'never fail when services look different,' because this is a real healthcare-compliance product and a payor auditor reviewing the TP text alone (without the reviewer's own outside knowledge that 'school-based' means a different provider) legitimately wants the DOCUMENT ITSELF to establish that the services are distinct, not rely on an inference nobody reading just the TP could safely make. The right bar sits between the old (too strict: demands a literal differentiation SENTENCE) and a naive fix (too loose: pass whenever services merely sound different): PASS/not_checkable when the TP documents ENOUGH distinguishing detail about the other service ANYWHERE in the document -- setting (school vs. home/community), provider type, or funding mechanism (IEP vs. this authorization) -- to make the services structurally distinguishable from that text alone, even without a dedicated sentence framed as 'ABA differs from X because...'. Concrete PASS example (this round's confirmed case): the TP's Biopsychosocial or Other Services section states the client 'receives school-based Speech/OT services through her IEP' while ABA is described as home-based -- setting and funding mechanism alone establish the distinction, no explicit differentiation sentence needed. FAIL only when either (a) the TP never establishes ANY distinguishing detail about the other service anywhere -- just 'also receives Speech/OT' with no setting/provider/scope information at all, or (b) the overlap is GENUINELY ambiguous even with full context -- same setting, same time window, unclear which goals belong to which service -- which is the one case that still needs an explicit differentiation statement because no other information in the document resolves it.

rules.description: POS correct (home/office/school/community only)
rules.notes: Enum validation — valid values are exactly: home, office, school, community. Reclassified from deterministic to judgment (2026-07): three rounds of point-fixes each closed one specific false-match pattern (mid-word regex matches, then a blank field bleeding into the next label, then a still-unresolved case) without addressing the underlying issue — this field's real-world layout/labeling in the source PDF is too inconsistent for a fixed extraction pattern to hold up. Read the POS/place-of-service field directly from the document text and images and judge whether its value is one of the four valid options above; do not guess if the field itself is ambiguous or missing. WHICH POS SOURCE, EXPLICIT (2026-08-07, Round 64, item 2 -- confirmed real divergence: this rule and QA-GIP-09, judged in the exact same run against the exact same document, disagreed about whether Community was an authorized POS, because nothing told either rule which of TWO different 'POS' fields a real TP contains to read. A TP's School/ABA Schedule grid has its OWN 'POS' row -- that's only the SPECIFIC location(s) actually scheduled that particular week (e.g. Home on weekdays), which can be a narrower subset of what's authorized. The Hours Requesting section separately states each CPT code's AUTHORIZED place(s) of service (e.g. '97153-Direct Care ... Home, Office, and/or Community') -- this is the broader, authorizing statement, and is the correct source for THIS rule and for QA-GIP-09/QA-GIP-08. Read POS from the Hours Requesting section's stated authorized list, not the schedule grid's per-day POS row -- the schedule grid answers a different question (where sessions are actually happening this week), not this rule's question (what POS is this TP authorized for). SCOPE, EXPLICIT -- EVERY SERVICE CODE, NOT JUST 97153 (2026-08-08, Round 78, item 2 -- real miss confirmed against Ms. Yachnes's ground-truth review: 'Telehealth' was listed as an authorized POS for 97151, 97155, and 97156 on a real TP, and this rule passed anyway because it only evaluated 97153's own POS entry, never looking at the OTHER service codes' entries in the same Hours Requesting section). The Hours Requesting section lists an authorized POS value PER CPT code (97151, 97153, 97154, 97155, 97156, etc., however many the document lists) -- read and validate EVERY one of these code-level POS entries against the four allowed categories, not only 97153's. Fail if ANY listed code's authorized POS includes a value outside home/office/school/community (e.g. 'Telehealth', 'Virtual', or anything else not one of the four) -- name which specific code(s) had the invalid value in the evidence, don't just say 'POS is incorrect' generically. Only treat this as pass if EVERY code's own POS entry is valid; a single invalid code among several valid ones is still a fail for this rule.

rules.description: At least 2 each of social/communication/behavior, narrative format
rules.notes:
There is no separate DET count check for this rule -- the LLM alone must both classify AND count. Concretely: for each of the 3 buckets (Social, Communication, Behavior) find the 'Problem Area:' entries listed under that bucket's heading, and for each one check whether it has an actual 'As evidenced by:' narrative statement attached (a specific behavioral description, not a blank). An entry whose 'As evidenced by:' is missing, blank, or literally 'n/a' does NOT count toward the 2-per-bucket minimum -- it is an unevidenced problem area, not a documented one. Fail if any of the 3 buckets has fewer than 2 entries with real evidenced narrative. (Confirmed failure mode: a Behavior bucket with 4 listed 'Problem Area:' items but one item's 'As evidenced by:' is 'n/a' -- that item must be excluded from the count, and if excluding it drops any bucket below 2, this is a fail even though the bucket looked fully populated at a glance.)

Converted from judgment to deterministic (2026-07-28 round, item 4): diagnosed as a real, previously-unfixed bug -- see pipeline/fields.py::_check_ACF07 for the full real-evidence diagnosis on both documents (Charny: entire Assessment of Current Functioning section blank, with an explicit reviewer annotation asking for it to be filled in; Reeda: ABLLS-R dated, but Vineland-3 data present with no administration date and its own embedded reviewer question asking exactly that -- 'Is the Vineland for this auth? What was the date of administration...'). The real check is: every named testing tool must have a confirmed Assessment Date tying it to a specific authorization period, or the section must not be entirely blank. Both are checkable from the TP's own text. Verified live: both real documents correctly come back fail. CLARIFIED (2026-08-06, Round 63, item 4 -- confirmed by Ms. Yachnes's own ground-truth read): 'old and new testing tool' does NOT require two DIFFERENT instruments. It is equally satisfied by the SAME tool administered twice on two different dates (an old score and a new score from one instrument) -- that is a completely normal, common re-administration pattern, not a gap. Two different tools, each dated once, still also satisfies it. What actually fails this rule is: the section is blank, a named tool has no confirmed administration date, or exactly one tool is named with only one confirmed date (in that last case: 'uncertain', not a guessed pass or fail -- a second administration may simply not be documented yet, not confirmed absent).

FIXED (2026-08, Round 83, item 1): confirmed real symptom -- this rule declared the whole section 'entirely blank' on a document where QA-ACF-01/QA-ACF-05's own separate reads found the date/summary fine in the same run. Root cause: pipeline/fields.py::_find_acf_section committed to the FIRST occurrence of the section header, which mis-scopes the section on any document where that heading text appears more than once before the real section (most plausibly a Table of Contents/outline page). Fixed to prefer whichever occurrence's captured slice actually contains a recognized ACF field label; this rule's own 'entirely blank' check also now cross-checks the whole document before confidently declaring blank, downgrading to 'uncertain' if the fields exist elsewhere (a likely boundary miss, not a real blank section). Could not reproduce against the exact original document -- none of this project's three locally available real TPs has an image-only page anywhere -- so this is verified via direct code investigation, a constructed synthetic reproduction of the confirmed symptom shape, and confirmation all three real documents are unaffected/unchanged.

rules.description: Completed with clear and detailed rationale
rules.notes:
Concrete rubric added (2026-07-28 follow-up round, item 3 -- 'Quick' bucket): a passing Clinical Interpretation/rationale must (1) name the client's specific presenting concerns or assessment findings (not generic boilerplate that could apply to any patient), and (2) explicitly connect those findings to the specific interventions/goals chosen. PASS example: 'Given Reeda's significant delays in functional communication and elopement-related safety concerns identified during the ABLLS-R and Vineland assessments, intensive ABA services targeting mand training and safety awareness are clinically indicated.' FAIL example: 'The client requires ABA services to address her needs and improve her skills.' -- generic, names no specific finding or client detail, could be copy-pasted into any TP. Still expect a meaningful 'Uncertain' rate on genuinely borderline cases between these two poles -- this rubric narrows the range, it doesn't eliminate judgment entirely.

RECALIBRATED (2026-08, Round 82, item 3): confirmed real case -- a narrative explained that response to treatment 'could not be assessed... no direct ABA sessions were provided' due to a documented staffing gap, and this rule failed it as too generic. Investigated: the two-pole rubric above only describes 'real clinical justification for the goals chosen' vs 'vague boilerplate' -- it has NO category for a THIRD, genuinely different shape: a specific, situation-grounded explanation of why there is no clinical-progress narrative to give this period, citing a documented external cause (staffing gap, authorization lapse, family-caused cancellations, etc.). That gap in the rubric, not the original grader, was the real defect -- a narrative citing a specific, checkable, external reason is NOT the same failure mode as boilerplate that names no real detail; it just answers a different, equally legitimate question. Added third category, PASS/not_checkable (not fail): a narrative is NOT generic when it (a) states a specific, checkable reason no direct services/data exist this period (a named cause: staffing, authorization, family scheduling -- not just 'unable to assess' with nothing behind it), even if it names no clinical assessment findings, because there IS nothing to assess yet. Still FAIL a narrative that gives NO reason at all ('progress could not be determined' with nothing further) -- that remains indistinguishable from boilerplate. This does not loosen the original two-pole rubric for a document that DOES have session data to interpret -- a real progress narrative is still held to the same bar as before, and pure boilerplate on a document with real session data still fails.

PASS example (confirmed real phrasing this engagement, Charny's TP): 'Charny struggles to try new things or complete a task that is less preferred and this can serve as a barrier to session.' FAIL example: a Barriers to Treatment section that is blank, or reads only 'N/A' with no actual barrier-type statement anywhere in the document (not just this one section -- some documents describe a barrier elsewhere, e.g. in Biopsychosocial narrative, without it being duplicated into this specific section).

rules.description: Age-appropriate mastery criteria for behavior targets
rules.notes:
UNBLOCKED (2026-08, Round 81, item 3) -- this rule now HAS a concrete, confirmed real failure example, closing the 'no concrete failure example on record yet' gap below. Confirmed directly against a real document: a goal's own Target Name states "fewer than 1 occurrence" while that SAME goal's own Mastery Criteria field states "1-2 occurrences" -- a direct, same-goal-block numeric contradiction, needing zero clinical judgment to catch, just a cross-field comparison. See pipeline/fields.py::_check_BIP05 -- a HYBRID checker (same shape as QA-PROB-02, see that rule's own notes for the precedent): it deterministically catches ONLY this specific same-goal numeric-threshold contradiction (extracting a 'fewer than N'/'near 0'/range/bare-N occurrence ceiling from both the goal's Target Name and its own Mastery Criteria field, per goal block); when no goal states a comparable numeric threshold on both sides, or when they're stated but don't contradict, it returns not_checkable so the broader, genuinely subjective judgment call below still runs.

Original working standard (2026-07-28, still the real judgment-layer instruction for everything this DET pre-check doesn't catch): treat the criteria below as the working standard, not a confirmed-bug fix. Check the behavior target's stated Mastery Criteria (not just the goal wording) against the client's age and the behavior's own severity/safety profile: (a) for a safety-relevant behavior (elopement, aggression, self-injury), a strict zero-occurrence criterion is normal and NOT itself a fail; (b) flag only when the criterion is developmentally mismatched in a way you can point to in the text -- e.g. a criterion phrased for a skill far beyond the client's documented developmental/cognitive level, a criterion with no duration/session-count qualifier at all (just a bare percentage with no consistency window), or a criterion that ignores a stated generalization requirement (e.g. across settings/people) that the rest of the plan otherwise expects. Do not fail solely because a criterion sounds strict for a young child -- strictness alone is not the defect; an unexplained mismatch between the criterion's demand and the client's documented profile is.

INVESTIGATED, NOT FORCED (2026-08, Round 83, item 2c): a new real case had the same goal's Mastery Criteria stated two different ways in two different SECTIONS of the document; self-consistency landed on 'uncertain' rather than a confident fail. Honest finding: this DET checker's per-block scope cannot see a second mention living outside a Target Goal/Target Name block entirely (e.g. restated in unstructured BIP narrative prose) -- that shape needs the judgment layer's own text-matching, same as QA-GIP-05's notes describe for cross-section differently-worded comparisons, not a deterministic guess at an unconfirmed structure. Added ONE safe, narrow generalization: the SAME numeric-ceiling comparison now also fires when the same (formatting-normalized) goal name is repeated as a SECOND full Target Goal/Target Name block with a different Mastery Criteria ceiling -- covers the sub-case that's still genuinely structural, at zero added false-positive risk. Does NOT claim to resolve the narrative-restatement shape; 'uncertain' remains the honest answer there.

UNBLOCKED (2026-08, Round 82, item 2): converted from judgment to deterministic -- this rule's real bar is pure presence detection ('is a current level indicated at all, even informally'), which is fully pattern-extractable, same shape as QA-PPI-02/03/05 and QA-GIP-10/16. Original concrete example (2026-07-28 follow-up round, item 3 -- 'Quick' bucket, still accurate): PASS example (confirmed real phrasing this engagement, Reeda's TP): 'Behavior: Tantrum ... Current Level: 2x daily.' FAIL example: a behavior target block with Baseline stated but no 'Current Level:' value filled in anywhere for that behavior.

FIXED (2026-08, Round 87, item 1): confirmed real bug -- this checker only ever recognized the literal 'Current Level:' label, but real templates write this same field as 'Current Data:' just as often, sometimes exclusively. Confirmed on Yisroel Leibowitz's real document: all four real Behavior Reduction goals use 'Current Data:' (never 'Current Level:' once) with real values, and this rule failed all four despite the ground-truth reviewer explicitly crediting them as Pass ('Current Data is provided for all four behavior targets'). Also confirmed the same missing-label mechanism on Zohan Hossain's real document (though that document's one Behavior Reduction goal's own Current Data value is a genuine bare, unexplained N/A, so its correct verdict is still fail -- the fix corrects the EVIDENCE TEXT there from a misleading 'no value filled in' to the accurate 'bare, unexplained N/A', without changing that one goal's already-correct fail). Now treats 'Current Level:'/'Current Data:' as equivalent labels -- same naming-inconsistency shape already fixed for 'Target Name:'/'Target Goal:' in earlier rounds.

rules.description: All goals match the POS
rules.notes: Concrete example added (2026-07-28 follow-up round, item 3 -- 'Quick' bucket; NOT a DET-conversion candidate -- see QA-SCH-08's own notes for why this field's real-world layout is too inconsistent for a fixed extraction pattern, confirmed against real documents in an earlier round). CORRECTED (2026-08-07, Round 63, item 8 -- confirmed real bug: this rule was passing goals that state no setting information at all, on the theory that 'no goal names a CONFLICTING setting' = compliant. That's wrong: goals saying NOTHING about setting is an inability to confirm compliance, not evidence of it, and must not default to pass.) Three distinct outcomes, not two: (1) PASS -- at least one goal's own narrative affirmatively states a setting, and every goal that states one is consistent with the declared Place of Service (e.g. POS is Office/Home/Telehealth/Community, and a goal reading 'client will complete the task across settings including office and home' names only setting(s) POS covers). (2) FAIL -- ANY goal's narrative names a setting the declared POS does NOT cover (e.g. POS is 'Office' only, but a goal reads 'client will complete the task in the community setting' or 'at home without BT present'). (3) NOT_CHECKABLE -- no goal anywhere in the document states any setting/POS information at all; this is a genuine inability to confirm the goals match the POS, not a clean pass by default. Do not collapse (3) into (1) just because there's no explicit conflict -- absence of a stated conflict is not the same as confirmed compliance. WHICH POS SOURCE, EXPLICIT (2026-08-07, Round 64, item 2 -- same fix applied to QA-GIP-09/QA-SCH-08 after a confirmed real divergence between those two rules over this exact ambiguity): read the 'declared Place of Service' above from the Hours Requesting section's stated authorized place(s) of service per CPT code, NOT the School/ABA Schedule grid's per-day POS row -- the schedule grid shows only where sessions are actually scheduled this particular week, a real, potentially narrower subset of what's authorized, and is the wrong source for this rule's own POS comparison.

FAIL example: POS includes Community, but no goal anywhere in the document mentions community/generalization-across-settings at all. If POS doesn't include Community, not_applicable. WHICH POS SOURCE, EXPLICIT (2026-08-07, Round 64, item 2 -- confirmed real bug: this rule returned not_applicable, reasoning Community wasn't authorized, by reading only the School/ABA Schedule grid's own 'POS' row -- while QA-SCH-08, judged in the SAME run against the SAME document, correctly found Community authorized straight from the Hours Requesting section. Same document, same underlying fact, contradictory conclusions.): read Place of Service from the SAME source as QA-SCH-08 -- the Hours Requesting section's stated authorized place(s) of service per CPT code (e.g. '97153-Direct Care ... Home, Office, and/or Community'), NOT the School/ABA Schedule grid's per-day POS row. The schedule grid only shows which specific location(s) sessions are actually happening at THIS week -- a real, potentially narrower subset of what's authorized -- and is the wrong source for 'does POS include Community' questions in this rule or QA-SCH-08/QA-GIP-08.

rules.notes: Converted from judgment to deterministic (2026-07-28 round, item 1): this is a uniqueness/consistency check over a code-extractable list of per-goal field values, not a holistic reasoning task -- see pipeline/fields.py::_check_GIP10 for the implementation and its full rationale. Splits the document on every 'Target Goal:' marker (goals can span a page boundary), then for each goal block with a 'Sampling Method:' field checks: (a) the value matches a known method name (catches both a broken merge-field artifact like literal 'Page' and spelling/wording variants like 'Precent correct' or 'percentage correct'); (b) Baseline and Mastery Criteria are non-blank (catches a goal with a valid Sampling Method but a missing companion field). Verified live against both Reeda's and Charny's real documents against the already-known outliers: Reeda -- page 32 'Precent correct' (typo), page 37 'Page' (broken merge field), page 52 'percentage correct' (wording variant); Charny -- page 27, a Frequency-sampled goal with a blank Mastery Criteria. All four were correctly caught; no false positives on either document's other 30+ goals.

rules.description: Goals in behavioral context (SD, setting, expected response)
rules.notes: No confirmed failure example on record yet -- treat as the working standard, not a confirmed-bug fix. A passing goal's Target Goal text must contain, explicitly or unambiguously implied, all 3 elements: (1) an SD/antecedent condition -- what cues or triggers the behavior (e.g. 'when told no', 'when a demand is given', 'when BT is distracted'); (2) a setting/context if the goal is context-dependent (e.g. 'in a conversation', 'during a task'); (3) an expected response stated as an observable action, not a vague internal state (e.g. 'will mand by calling BT's name' is fine; 'will feel less anxious' is not, because there's no observable response). Fail when the antecedent condition is entirely missing (the goal reads as a bare behavior with no stated trigger) or when the expected response is an internal/emotional state with no observable action attached -- not merely because the goal is short.

rules.description: Mastery criteria age/ASD-appropriate; no 0%, use 'fewer than one instance'
rules.notes:
Converted from judgment to deterministic (2026-07-28 round, item 1 backlog): the zero/near-zero-endpoint ban is a per-goal pattern check over an extractable field (Mastery Criteria), same shape as GIP-10 -- see pipeline/fields.py::_check_GIP16, which shares GIP-10's _goal_block_starts helper. Scope note: this DET check covers ONLY the zero-value-ban half of the rule's description ('no 0%, use fewer than one instance'); the broader 'age/ASD-appropriate' framing in the description is not separately implemented here since no distinct check for it was ever built or described beyond the zero-ban itself -- if a genuinely separate age-appropriateness judgment is intended beyond the zero-ban, that would need its own rule/check. This ban applies to BOTH percentage-based AND frequency-based mastery criteria - do not treat frequency/count goals as exempt just because they don't use a percent sign. A mastery criterion is a violation if it states a zero or near-zero endpoint in ANY of these forms: '0%', '0 occurrences', '0x', 'near 0 levels', 'near 0', or equivalent zero-value phrasing - regardless of Sampling Method (Percent Correct or Frequency). Any of these must instead read 'fewer than one instance' (or an equivalent minimum-occurrence phrasing). Verified live: Reeda has exactly 2 confirmed violations (page 26 Tantrum, page 27 Elopement, both in 'Target Name:' Behavior Reduction Goal blocks -- not 'Target Goal:' ones, which is why the shared block-splitter covers both marker forms). Charny has zero violations (one goal reads '0-2 occurrences over three consecutive days', correctly NOT flagged since it's a range, not a zero endpoint). EXPLICIT DIVISION OF LABOR WITH QA-GIP-10 (2026-08-07, Round 63, item 7): a BLANK Mastery Criteria is a real problem, but this rule's own zero/near-zero pattern never matches an empty string, so on its own this would silently pass a blank field -- QA-GIP-10 already flags a blank Mastery Criteria, but ONLY for a goal block that also has a Sampling Method field (it skips any block without one). This rule now flags the one remaining gap -- a blank Mastery Criteria in a block with NO Sampling Method field either -- and deliberately does NOT also flag the Sampling-Method-present case, to avoid two rules reporting the same blank-field violation as if it were two separate problems. If both this rule and QA-GIP-10 pass on the same document, that means every Mastery Criteria field found is confirmed non-blank; a not_checkable from either is not itself evidence of a blank field.

BROADENED (2026-08, Round 83, item 2a): confirmed real miss -- '0 times a week' is the same absolute-zero problem as '0%', just phrased with 'times' instead, and the prior pattern didn't recognize it. _ZERO_MASTERY_PATTERN now also catches '0/zero times', '0/zero occurrences', '0/zero instances', and a bare '0'/'zero'/'none' as the field's entire value. Still deliberately does NOT match 'fewer than N'/'less than N' for any N -- that phrasing is this rule's own recommended non-zero rewording, not a violation.

rules.description: Goals observable/measurable with SD, deficit, expectation
rules.notes: Same family as GIP-11 -- same caution: no confirmed failure example on record yet, working standard only. A passing goal must contain: (1) an SD/antecedent condition (what prompts the target); (2) a deficit statement -- what the client currently cannot do or does incorrectly, stated concretely enough that progress against it is measurable; (3) an expectation stated as an observable, countable action (percent correct, count, duration -- not a vague internal-state description). Fail when the goal is observable/measurable in form (has a Mastery Criteria percentage) but the Target Goal text itself never states what deficit is being remediated, or when the antecedent condition is missing entirely -- a goal can have a perfectly quantitative Mastery Criteria and still fail this rule if the goal statement itself doesn't establish what's being measured and why.

rules.description: 3+ parent training goals/auth period, no 'caregiver' wording (or rationale if used)
rules.notes:
Three independent criteria, all must hold -- confirmed via real evidence on multiple documents that a compressed one-line description let these slip past unnoticed:
(1) At least 3 distinct parent-training goals exist for THIS authorization period. Count only goals under 'Goals in Progress' / currently active for this auth period -- do NOT count goals listed under 'Mastered Goals' toward this total, even if they use parent-training wording, since those are from a prior period. (Confirmed failure mode: a document with 4 'Mastered Goals' phrased as parent-training goals but only 1 actually current/in-progress goal -- the '3+' requirement is about the current period, and miscounting mastered history toward it produces a false pass.)
(2) No individual CURRENT goal's own Target Goal text uses 'caregiver' as its subject (e.g. 'The caregiver will...') instead of 'parent'/'parents'/'mother'/'father', unless that specific goal has its own accompanying rationale for the wording choice. IMPORTANT: this document type routinely uses 'Parent/Caregiver' as standard SECTION-HEADER and narrative terminology (e.g. 'Parent/Caregiver Involvement:', 'Parent/Caregiver Goals:', 'caregivers are coached on...') -- that widespread usage is NOT itself a violation of THIS sub-criterion and must not be read as making 'caregiver' wording normal everywhere in the document. This specific check is narrower: does any individual CURRENT goal's own subject specifically say 'caregiver' while its sibling current goals say 'parent(s)'/'mother'/'father'? That specific inconsistency, without a rationale for that one goal, is a fail under this sub-criterion.
(3) FIXED (2026-08-08, Round 78, item 1 -- closes the cross-section gap flagged as a known limitation in Round 63; real miss confirmed on Yisroel Leibowitz's real TP, where foster care is noted under Biopsychosocial Information but the Parent/Caregiver section's own generic header-level 'Parent/Caregiver' language carries no rationale anywhere in the document). Read the WHOLE document, not just this section, for any indication that the child's caregiver is NOT a biological/legal parent -- foster care, kinship care, a non-parent guardian, a grandparent raising the child, a group-home placement, or any other stated non-parent caregiving arrangement, wherever it appears (commonly Biopsychosocial Information or Educational History, but check anywhere). Do not key this off the single literal phrase 'foster care' -- recognize the underlying fact pattern (someone other than the child's parent is the caregiver) however it's actually phrased. If such an indication IS present anywhere in the document: a rationale for using 'Parent/Caregiver' / generic 'caregiver' language (instead of naming the specific relationship, e.g. 'foster parent' or 'grandparent/guardian') must appear SOMEWHERE reasonably tied to that language -- in the Parent/Caregiver section itself, or elsewhere explaining the choice. Its absence is a fail under this sub-criterion, even if criteria (1) and (2) both pass and even if the document's 'Parent/Caregiver' phrasing is only ever used at the section-header/narrative level (which sub-criterion (2) above treats as normal in the ordinary case -- this sub-criterion is the deliberate exception for when a real non-parent-caregiver fact is on record elsewhere). If NO such indication is found anywhere in the document, this sub-criterion is satisfied by default (nothing to justify) -- do not fail a document with no stated non-parent-caregiver fact just because it uses 'Parent/Caregiver' as ordinary header language.
COUNTING SCOPE (confirmed second false-pass mechanism, on a document where the mastered-goals exclusion above was already applied correctly): only count entries listed literally under a 'Parent/Caregiver Goals:' (or equivalent parent-training goal list) heading for the current period. A 'Transition Plan' / hours-titration section that discusses parent training being 'mastered and maintained' in its narrative, or that lists the PATIENT's own skill-mastery criteria in a numbered table (e.g. 'When [patient] can make 5 relevant comments...'), is not a parent-training goal and must not be counted toward the 3+ total just because it sits near parent-training language or references future parent-training phases. If, after excluding both Mastered Goals and any non-goal-list narrative/tables, fewer than 3 distinct current parent-training goals remain, this is a fail regardless of how much surrounding text discusses parent involvement generally.

CLARIFIED (2026-08, Round 85, item 2): confirmed real miss on Blythe Diaz's TP -- the required 3 Program Goals correctly use 'Parent,' but the document also has additional SUPPLEMENTAL parent-training-adjacent goals beyond those 3 that happen to use 'Caregiver' wording; the ground-truth reviewer's own standard is a clean Pass here, since those extra goals are beyond the required minimum and their wording doesn't affect it. Sub-criterion (2) above, read literally, never said this -- it just said 'No individual CURRENT goal's own Target Goal text uses caregiver,' with no distinction between the (up to) 3 goals actually being counted toward the minimum and any supplemental goals beyond it. That ambiguity is corrected here: sub-criterion (2)'s caregiver-wording check applies ONLY to the goals actually being counted toward the 3+ minimum (the same set counted for sub-criterion (1)) -- a supplemental goal beyond that minimum using 'Caregiver' wording, with no rationale, does NOT violate sub-criterion (2) and does not affect the pass. If choosing which (up to) 3 goals count is itself ambiguous (e.g. more than 3 parent-training goals exist and it's unclear which are 'the required 3'), prefer the reading that credits the document -- a genuine, unambiguous violation still requires an identifiable specific goal using unrationaled 'caregiver' wording among the goals needed to reach the minimum, not merely SOME goal somewhere in the document doing so.

rules.description: Patient-specific and realistic based on goals
rules.notes:
'Matches the Learning Tree' wording ignored per Section 14. The real check here is NOT a general judgment call on goal specificity/realism (that's a fallback only) — the manual reviewer's own embedded note asks for a status sentence on every Transition Plan goal, and it isn't there. Look for a reviewer-embedded comment/highlighted annotation near the Transition Plan section requesting a status update on Transition Plan goals (the same kind of embedded PDF annotation as a severity-rating note elsewhere in this rule set). If that reviewer note is present: check every individual Transition Plan goal in the document for a short status sentence attached to it, and fail if any goal lacks one — this is a per-goal presence check, not a subjective realism judgment. If no such reviewer note is present anywhere near the Transition Plan section, fall back to the general judgment call on whether goals are patient-specific and realistic.

INVESTIGATED, ALREADY CORRECT (2026-08, Round 84, item 2): re-examined as part of an audit for rules that dress up an unverifiable external-source claim as a confident pass. Found this rule does NOT have that problem -- 'matches the Learning Tree' was already explicitly retired as dead scope by Section 14 (see also QA-ACF-05's own notes, which retired the same wording for a different checklist item the same way). The fallback general realism judgment above is this rule's own genuine, full scope once the reviewer-note check comes up empty -- not a stand-in for an unavailable harder comparison -- so a confident pass/fail from that fallback is appropriate, not overconfident. No change made here.
